The applicant has filed this First bail application under Section 482 of BNSS/438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.32/2026 registered at Police Station Dehat, District Vidisha (M.P.) in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 420, 406 and 34 of IPC.
2.

As per prosecution story, on 05.12.2025, the complainant, Radharaman Ahirwar--a resident of Ward No. 34, Durganagar, Vidisha, and Director of Suryavanshi Traders--submitted a written application to the Station House Officer (SHO), Civil Lines Police Station, Vidisha.

The registered office of Suryavanshi Traders is located on NH 146, Village NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 2 MCRC-13020-2026 Dhakna Chakna, Sanchi, District Raisen, situated in front of the Maithil Dhaba Kaya Spirits Unit of Bacchus Enterprises Limited.

The corporate identification number for the entity is 051909 PB 1994 PLC 014656.
3.

To secure a liquor dealership for the Madhya Pradesh State (Bhopal Depot) through a mediator,
Rajneesh Kumar, the complainant met with several parties.
On 15.04.2022, Rajneesh Kumar and Karun Kaura (the present applicant) received Rs. 5,00,000/-.
The complainant was then called to an office in Patiala, where he met Shashikala and Roop Handa.

After being presented with lucrative Karun Kaura vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113382058/
1 offers and margin terms, he was introduced to the CMD of the company.

sentences.text: Following the meeting with Karun Kaura, a franchise fee of Rs. 30,00,000/- for the Bhopal depot was settled.
An agreement was executed in the Patiala Court on 29.04.2022 through Advocate Rajinder K. Ahuja between Kaya Spirits and the complainant.
The agreement stipulated the delivery of goods within 45 days.
On 29.04.2022, the complainant transferred Rs. 25,00,000/- via RTGS from his Bank of India account (Sanchi Branch, A/c No. 949220110000037) to Kaya Spirits' account (A/c No. 01625501230).

The remaining Rs. 5,00,000/- was paid via a Post-Dated Cheque (PDC) drawn on the Bank of India,
Sanchi Branch, in favor of Kaya Spirits Pvt. Ltd.
Of this total Rs. 30,00,000/-, Rs. 15,00,000/- was contributed by the complainant's partner, Kishanlal Ladia, and Rs. 15,00,000/- was contributed by the complainant himself.
When the goods were not delivered to the Bhopal depot within 45 days, the complainant contacted Karun Kaura via telephone and email.

Kaura instructed the complainant to meet him at the Okhla office, where the complainant met NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 3 MCRC-13020-2026 with Manager Manpreet, Shashikala, and Roop Handa.
They discussed bottling operations in Himachal but failed to provide the necessary documentation, claiming it would be sent later.
On 22.06.2022, Karun Kaura again summoned the complainant to Patiala and proposed a partnership for the entire state of Madhya Pradesh.
Kaura claimed that a total investment of Rs. 1.5 crore would be required, for which Rs. 75,00,000/- worth of goods would be provided.

After accounting for the Rs. 35,00,000/- already considered deposited,
Kaura instructed the complainant to arrange an additional Rs. 40,00,000/-.

Subsequently, the complainant collected funds from several firms, including; Shri R.J. Ram Chandra Traders (Vidisha), Shri Mahesh Chaudhary Brothers Enterprises (Raisen), Shri Pradeep Thakur Ananda Traders (Rajgarh), Sachin Kumar Chaudhary & Sons Enterprises (Indore).
4.
On 22.06.2022, Karun Kaura executed a franchise agreement for the entire state and continued to solicit payments of Rs. 5-10 lakhs under the guise of "work-level" expenses.
By 02.09.2022, a total of Rs. 75,00,000/- had been paid to Kaya Spirits through cash and bank transfers.

On 10.09.2022,
Manpreet Kaur demanded an additional Rs. 5,00,000/-.
When the complainant refused and instead demanded the delivery of the promised goods, the behavior of Karun Kaura and Roop Handa changed.
They began sending irrelevant emails, leading the complainant to suspect fraud.
The complainant attempted to contact the four individuals, but found that their phones were switched off.

Upon gathering further information regarding Kaya Spirits & Distilleries, the complainant discovered that Karun Kaura had NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 4 MCRC-13020-2026 allegedly defrauded another individual--Dilip Garg, a resident of Gwalior-- of 1,00,00,000 (One Crore) in a similar manner.
On the basis of these facts, the aforementioned FIR was registered against the present applicant (Karun Kaura) and the other co-accused persons.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence.
It is further submitted that present FIR is false & frivolous and of civil nature/flavour and thus, is liable to be quashed at the outset.

The same has been lodged by the Complainant/ Respondent no. 2 herein i.e., Mr. Radharaman Ahirwar, against the Applicant/Accused for converting civil dispute into criminal complaint and to settle his scores and thereby causing undue hardship and difficulties for the Applicant/Accused, by unnecessarily dragging him in the present criminal case, for the ulterior motives to browbeat the Applicant so that he succumbs to illegal demands of Respondent no. 2.

Counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to MOU dated 28.04.2022, wherein,
"Applicable Law and Settlement of Disputes." provides that any and all disputes arising out of or in relation to the Agreement, including issues relating to performance, non-performance. breach,
termination, invalidity or interpretation, shall be referred to a sole arbitrator to be appointed mutually by the parties in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
1996.
The seat and venue of arbitration is stipulated to be Patiala, Punjab, India.

It is further clarified that in respect of applications made under the Arbitration and Conciliation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 5 MCRC-13020-2026 Act, 1996, the Courts at Patiala alone shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, there exists an efficacious alternative remedy of arbitration for resolution of disputes.
However.
merely to give a colour of criminality to a purely civil dispute, the Complainant has chosen to initiate the present criminal proceedings against the applicant.

The Complainant himself executed an undertaking stating that due to unavoidable circumstances, he, namely Mr. Radha Raman Ahirwar, along with his partners/agents of M/s Suryawanshi Traders, could not start operations in the State of Madhya Pradesh, though M/s Kaya Blenders & Distillers Ltd. had already executed and commenced its part of the operations by getting the labels approved and dispatching the material in fulfillment of the terms and conditions of the Agreement.

In the said undertaking, the Complainant further stated that he and his partners/agents had no dispute with M/s Kaya Spirits Unit of Bacchus Enterprises Ltd.. M/s Bacchus Enterprises Ltd., M/s Kaya Blenders & Distillers Ltd., and Mr. Karun Kaura, and assured full cooperation in carrying on the business smoothly as per the Agreement dated 22.06.2022.
Despite the undertaking and the State Franchisee & Bottling Partner Agreement dated 22.06.2022, the Complainant failed to perform his obligations.

He did not obtain the requisite excise permissions in time, failed to deposit required duties and charges, did not lift the minimum guaranteed stock, and did not commence operations in the State of Madhya Pradesh.
It is further submitted that the dispute escalated not because of any deception on the part of the Applicant, but solely due to nonperformance by the Complainant,

Instead of fulfilling his commitments, the Complainant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 6 MCRC-13020-2026 (Partners) resorted to threatening and abusive conduct.
The Applicant's Company was compelled to issue a legal notice dated 16.11.2022 calling upon the Complainant to cease unlawful conduct and honor his contractual obligations.

Thereafter,
on 21.11.2022, the Applicant lodged a complaint before the Special Commissioner of Police, Women & Children Wing.

entities.text: Special Commissioner of Police, Women & Children Wing
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Delhi, detailing incidents of threats, abusive language and criminal intimidation,
including against female staff members of the Company.
This complaint predates the FIR lodged by the Complainant and clearly reflects his deteriorating and mala fide conduct.
The present FIR is a gross abuse of the criminal process and arises out of a purely commercial and contractual dispute.
The entire relationship between the parties is governed by written agreements.
including the MOU dated 28.04.2022, the State Franchisee & Bottling Partner Agreement dated 22.06.2022 and the Addendum dated 27.05.2023.
Such issues are squarely civil in nature and cannot be given a criminal colour in the absence of dishonest intention at the inception of the transaction.

In such circumstances, Counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the judgments passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Naresh Kumar and Anr. Vs. State of Karnataka and Anr. [SLP (Crl) No. 1570 of 2021] and Anukul Singh Vs. State of U.P. and Anr. [SLP (Crl) No. 2682 of 2020].

sentences.text: He undertakes to fully cooperate with the investigation as well as the trial and assure that he shall make himself available before the investigating agency whenever required.
There is no likelihood of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 7 MCRC-13020-2026 applicant's absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, it is humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant in the interest of justice.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the State, as well as counsel for the Complainant, vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
They prayed for the rejection of the application, citing 12 criminal antecedents against the applicant.
It was submitted that the applicant's extensive criminal history clearly demonstrates a persistent pattern of criminal activity.
Furthermore, the applicant is currently absconding, and the investigation remains ongoing.
It is further submitted that the Case Diary contains sufficient material to implicate the applicant in the act of cheating the complainant.
Consequently, the applicant's plea that the matter is merely a "civil dispute" is sustainable neither in fact nor in law and offers no merit to the present application.
Given the gravity of the allegations, the applicant's prior criminal record, and his failure to cooperate with the investigating agency, the State and the Complainant pray for the dismissal 8.
Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

9. While the applicant contends that the dispute arises from a breach of contract, the allegations involving the inducement of large sums of money across multiple parties, coupled with the revelation of similar alleged frauds elsewhere, suggest a prima facie case of criminal intent rather than a mere commercial failure.

10. The Court notes with concern that the applicant has a significant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11027 8 MCRC-13020-2026 criminal history consisting of 12 antecedents.
Furthermore, the applicant has been reported as absconding, thereby hindering the progress of the investigation.

In cases involving substantial financial fraud and a history of similar offences, the need for custodial interrogation cannot be ruled out to uncover the trail of the alleged proceeds of crime.
11.

In view of the gravity of the offence, the criminal history of the applicant, and his conduct in evading the process of law, this Court is not inclined to grant the extraordinary relief of anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the application is hereby dismissed.

(RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA ) JUDGE (LJ*)
